claim.why_it_matters: Numbered subsection heading left as a plain paragraph, while siblings 2.10 (page 715) and 2.12 (page 717) are rendered '##'.

verdict.reasoning: The 300 dpi render of page 716 (folio XVII-8) prints '2.11  CODASYL COBOL JOURNAL OF DEVELOPMENT 1981' as a numbered subsection heading of the History of COBOL, set flush left on its own line like its siblings. The heading words are present and identical in the markdown (specs/ANSI_COBOL_1985.md line 26686), so no text is missing; the defect is that the line carries no heading marker, while '## 2.9' (26576), '## 2.10' (26632) and '## 2.12' (26756) of the same list are headings. The claim quotes both sources correctly. It is structural only: the section does not appear in the document outline, and no normative meaning changes. Sibling sweep: 2.5 (26480), 2.6 (26506), 2.7 (26532) and 2.8 (26548), the CODASYL JOD 1968 to 1973 headings, are plain paragraphs too, so the inconsistency covers the whole 2.x list, not only 2.11.
verdict.corrected_description: Accurate for 2.11: the heading text matches, but the markdown leaves it as a plain paragraph where the siblings 2.9, 2.10 and 2.12 are '##' headings. Structural only, with no change in meaning. The same defect affects 2.5 to 2.8 (lines 26480, 26506, 26532, 26548), which should be fixed together.
